input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. I traced every limitation of all 17 claims (independent claims 1, 11, 14 and dependent claims 2-10, 12-13, 15-17), all 28 entries of the numeral ledger (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 30-66) and each numbered part's use in the description and in every figure, all six figure briefs (FIG. 1-6) and the Brief Description of the Drawings, and the title, cross-reference, government-support, field, background, summary, detailed description, claims and abstract, against the affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER message in input/conversation.md. The invention substance traces cleanly: two semicircular frame halves with hinge and releasable latch; three jaw carriages in radial guides with pivoting concave jaw pads that need no tool-specific pipe diameter; a segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment carried by each half; complementary drive faces at the hinge end and the latch end that couple the segments on closure; followers in oblique slots producing synchronized inward travel; a wedge driven by the latch against a ring drive face through a limited stroke; carriage springs biasing each carriage outward; the first (holding) and second (over-center) latch positions; the force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge absorbing remaining travel; the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing over a predetermined compression range and reporting load rather than diameter; the install and remove sequences; and the mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in synchronization. Numeral-to-part mapping is one-to-one and consistent across the ledger, the description and every figure brief; every numeral listed on a figure is used in the description, and every described part carries the same numeral in every view (for example 54 is the ring drive face in both FIG. 3 and FIG. 4, and 44/46/48/50 keep upper-segment/lower-segment and left/hinge-end/right/latch-end assignments consistent with FIG. 1's hinge-left, latch-right and FIG. 3's upper/lower segments). No section lines are used, so no section designation mismatch arises; view names agree between each brief and the Brief Description of the Drawings. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in the draft, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language was added to the application text to justify a renderer's choice. I found two problems, both reported below: a functional-surface geometry statement in the FIG. 3 and FIG. 6 briefs that fixes the circumferential position of the ring drive face relative to the slots and to both segment junctions, which the inventor never states, and one untraced result clause in the detailed description. Note for the record: the YOU passage in input/conversation.md refers to a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface", which is agent prose about a different subject matter and is not inventor support; no such matter appears in the draft, and none of the draft's technical content rests on it. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced here, and no prior_art/ files were included in this material, so that tracing is left to the later citation review as instructed.

findings.title: Figure briefs fix the circumferential position of the ring drive face relative to the slots and both segment junctions, which the disclosure never states
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, "Geometry to draw" fourth bullet and numeral placement target for 54; figures/FIG-6.md, "Geometry to draw" last bullet
findings.detail: The ring drive face (54) is the functional face on which the wedge acts to rotate the coupled cam ring. FIG-3 places it circumferentially "clear of the slots and clear of both junctions", and FIG-6 repeats "clear of both junctions". That is a circumferential end-position statement about a functional drive face: it asserts that the wedge acts on the ring at a location spaced away from the latch-end junction (where the latch itself sits per FIG. 1) and away from every oblique slot. Under the functional-surface rule this is substantive even though the brief says the drive face is "shown schematically", and it is not a mere page placement or leader-collision constraint because it appears in the geometry to be drawn, not only in the numeral placement targets. The disclosure affirmatively discloses the face itself but says nothing about where it lies on the ring band relative to the slots or to the junctions.
findings.evidence: Candidate wording, FIG-3.md: "A short drive face is located on the ring band, at a place clear of the slots and clear of both junctions." and "54: the short drive face on the ring band, clear of both junctions." Candidate wording, FIG-6.md: "A drive face from FIG. 3 is shown schematically on the band, clear of both junctions, without a numeral." No affirmative inventor passage supports any circumferential position for this face. The nearest source passage is: "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke." (input/disclosure.md, second paragraph), which discloses the face and its function only. The related passage "When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring" locates the coupling faces at the junctions but says nothing about the ring drive face.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md replace the geometry bullet with: "- A short drive face is shown schematically on the ring band. Its position along the band is a drawing convention adopted only so that its leader does not collide with the other leaders, and conveys no particular circumferential relationship to the slots or to the junctions." and replace the numeral target with: "- 54: the short drive face on the ring band." In figures/FIG-6.md replace the corresponding bullet with: "- A drive face from FIG. 3 is shown schematically on the band, without a numeral, at the same conventional position used in FIG. 3." Make no change to the claims, the description or the Brief Description of the Drawings, none of which recite any position for the ring drive face.

findings.title: Untraced result clause: "without dismantling the drive"
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "The segmented cam ring", third paragraph
findings.detail: The clause states a result of the segmented construction that no inventor passage asserts. The inventor states only that one segment is carried by each frame half and that closure couples them; nothing in the disclosure or the conversation addresses dismantling, disassembly, or the absence of it when the frame is opened. The preceding clause of the same sentence ("Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened") is supported and can stand alone.
findings.evidence: Candidate wording: "Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive." Nearest source passages: "A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half." and "an operator opens the latch, swings the frame halves apart, places them around a pipe, closes the frame" (input/disclosure.md). Neither states any result about dismantling the drive.
findings.fix: Delete the trailing clause so the sentence reads: "Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened." No other section repeats the clause, so no further edits are required.
